record.original_question: Let {gamma_k}_{k>=0} be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that f(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/k! is an entire function. For parameters p with -p not in N, define the generalized Bessel-type function F_p(x)=sum_{k>=0} gamma_k x^k/(k! Gamma(k+p+1)). Characterize exactly which nonnegative sequences {gamma_k} make F_p belong to the Laguerre-Polya class of real entire functions.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Characterize all non-negative sequences {gamma_k}_0^infinity such that if f(x) = sum_{k=0}^infinity gamma_k x^k/k! is an entire function, then F_p(x) = sum_{k=0}^infinity gamma_k x^k/(k!Gamma(k + p + 1)) belongs to L - P, for -p notin N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Laguerre–Pólya class $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}$ consists of all real entire functions that are uniform limits, on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$, of real polynomials having only real zeros. Equivalently, a real entire function $\varphi$ belongs to $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}$ if and only if it admits a Hadamard factorization of the form
$$\varphi(z) = c\, z^m e^{-\alpha z^2 + \beta z}\prod_{k\ge 1}\left(1-\frac{z}{x_k}\right)e^{z/x_k},$$
with $c,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\ge 0$, $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, $x_k\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$, and $\sum_k x_k^{-2}<\infty$.

Let $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that the power series
$$f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{\gamma_k}{k!}\,x^k$$
defines an entire function. For a real parameter $p$ with $-p\notin\mathbb{N} = \{1,2,3,\dots\}$, define the associated generalized Bessel-type function
$$F_p(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{\gamma_k}{k!\,\Gamma(k+p+1)}\,x^k.$$

Give a complete characterization of all nonnegative sequences $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ (with $f$ entire) for which $F_p$ belongs to the Laguerre–Pólya class, for every $p$ with $-p\notin\mathbb{N}$.
